paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The image displays a donut chart with two concentric rings, illustrating the distribution of samples across different levels of ambiguity metrics. The outer ring represents the sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (Std), categorized into four segments: Std: 0.0 (darkest blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (medium-dark blue, 38.0%), Std: 0.82 (medium blue, 7.0%), and Std: 0.94 (light blue, 5.0%). The inner ring corresponds to the sample-level maximum ambiguity (Max), divided into three segments: Max: 1 (light blue, 39.0%), Max: 2 (lighter blue, 47.7%), and Max: 3 (very light blue, 14.2%). The chart includes two legends on the right: one for the outer ring labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” with four color-coded Std values, and one for the inner ring labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” with three color-coded Max values. Each segment is labeled with its percentage value directly on the chart, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right. The visual representation suggests that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity, as the largest segments in both rings correspond to the lowest Std and Max values.
